name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.17.0 — build's red-check (Phase 0 step 2's expected-colour classification plus Phase 1's hand-run reconciliation paragraph) is now mechanized by `spec/scripts/red-check.js` (`spec-paths red-check`), replacing prose with executed exit codes: expectation derives from `SHALL CONTINUE TO` pins and a new closed-enum `[pre-green: <reason>]` AC tag (`fallback-rejection` | `absence-invariant` | `predicate-in-test` — the three recorded sub-shapes of the class this spec closes); the script executes the host's own `{testCommand}`/`{typecheckCommand}` once per tests-layer file and reads exit codes only, never runner output, probing non-DELETE File Plan paths for existence before invoking the runner (a missing file would otherwise fake a satisfied red expectation) and refusing at exit 2 when any non-tests File Plan path already differs from the diff base, tracked or untracked. `lib/spec-sections.js`'s `parseAcBullets` gains the `preGreen` field and exports `PRE_GREEN_REASONS` as the single enum authority; `ac-matrix.js` counts valid tags into its typed manifest row (`observed.preGreen`) so the class rides every review ledger row fleet-countable, and rejects an out-of-enum reason as hard finding `invalid-pre-green` — the tag never launders coverage (a tagged AC with zero test hits still counts uncovered). The pipeline rules' thrice-amended vacuous-pin Gotchas paragraph (six recorded instances since 2026-08-17) shrinks to a one-line pointer at the script's incident header and its test file (JJ approved 2026-08-21). Deliberately NOT built (D12, rejected per core § Incident Policy): a mandatory per-AC mutation/kill-check — the class it would guard has zero recorded members across every ledger this repo can read, and `/spec:replay` already occupies that niche at a fraction of the cost; the tag remains a planner/worker attestation welded to execution, never a proof that the pinned assertion discriminates, which stays reviewer residue. 7.16.0 — a worktree review's `RED_BLOCKING` hard stop now writes its `GATE_RED` ledger line durably to the main root's gitignored `.claude/spec-runs.stopped.jsonl` at the moment of the stop instead of the worktree's own ledger, closing R3(1) deferred at spec 07's review: an abandoned or force-removed worktree could destroy the only record of a stopped attempt, since the row previously reached the main root only if a merge later landed. `spec-review-driver.js`'s hard-stop path self-provisions the ignore entry via git's `info/exclude` when the host lacks it (idempotent, worktree-shared — executed spike A5), and falls back loudly to today's worktree-local append when a host `.gitignore` negation pattern outranks `info/exclude` in git's precedence, naming the `.gitignore` remedy line in the STOPPED step text; the driver always names the absolute path the row landed in. `lib/observation.js`'s `readLedgerRows()` needed zero changes — it already union-merges `spec-runs*.jsonl` by filename order (executed spikes A1/A4) — so `spec-status`, `replay --due`, and `/spec:escape` see stopped rows with no reader edits. The rows drain back into the tracked ledger, positioned before the run's close row, when that spec later closes CLEAN — in-place or via merge promotion — through one spec-scoped helper called from both `promoteEvidenceAndClean()` and `doCloseWork()`. Deliberately NOT built: locking around the drain's read-modify-write window (accepted as the same order-of-magnitude race as every other multi-session ledger append this repo already lives with); extending the durable write to the CLOSE row; and a ledger row for ESCALATE, a pre-existing gap that writes no row today and stays explicitly out of scope. 7.15.1 — /spec:doctor's cited-reference check now extracts BARE FILENAMES, not just directory-prefixed paths. A path-shaped regex silently passes every directory-less citation, which is how `.claude/agents/doctrine-author.md` kept instructing every doctrine worker to add a row to `scaffold-ledger.md` — a file deleted in v7's `61e2e5a` delete-layer commit, whose function (dated justification, earned-under, mandatory retire condition) was absorbed and strengthened by core § Incident Policy's five-field bar. The stale rule is repointed at that bar; `.claude/rules/conventions/doctrine.md` had already carried the v7 wording, so the agent file was the twin the same commit did not sweep. Recorded at recurrence count one and deliberately NOT mechanized into a new sweep script: the miss was caught by eye in the same run, and core § Incident Policy earns a standing guard at a third recurrence, not a first.
